entry.title: I got tired of switching between 10 tabs while debugging… so I built this
entry.summary:
I got tired of switching between 10 tabs while debugging… so I built this
If you’ve worked with APIs, JSON, or tokens, you’ve probably had this moment: You start debugging something simple… JWT decoder JSON formatter Base64 encoder/decoder regex tester timestamp converter Before you realize it, you’ve got 8–10 tabs open. Each tool solves a tiny problem. context switching inconsistent interfaces slow or cluttered tools unnecessary mental overhead Individually, it’s fine. Instead of jumping between tools, I wanted something that: brings all essential developer utilities into one place is fast and responsive (no lag, no waiting) has a clean, distraction-free UI runs entirely in the browser (no data upload) Something that feels like a developer scratchpad, not a collection of random websites. I started small, just for my own workflow: JWT decoder JSON formatter Base64 tool timestamp converter Then I kept adding what I actually needed day-to-day: regex tester cURL → fetch / axios converters SQL formatter URL encoder/decoder hash generator (MD5, SHA) YAML ↔ JSON converters and more Over time, it turned into a full developer utility hub. 👉 I put everything here: https://timedev.ai Most tools online work — but don’t feel great to use. So I focused on a few things: Everything should feel instant. No loading, no friction. No ads, no clutter — just the tool. Everything runs locally in your browser. Nothing is uploaded. Same experience across all tools, so you don’t have to “relearn” anything. A few things I didn’t expect: How much time small context switches actually waste How inconsistent most dev tools feel How much smoother workflows become when everything is in one place I’m currently exploring: AI-assisted explanations (e.g., explain JSON, JWT payloads, regex patterns) expanding tool coverage further refining UX and performance Curious to hear from other devs: 👉 What’s the one tool you use every single day? I’m building this based on real workflows, so ideas matter a lot.
